impl<K: VectorKind> GradedVector<K>::add.body: { self.check_compatible(other)?; let coefficients = self .coefficients .iter() .zip(other.coefficients.iter()) .map(|(a, b)| a + b) .collect(); Ok(Self::from_canonical( self.degree, self.basis_id.clone(), coefficients, )) }
impl<K: VectorKind> GradedVector<K>::add.obligation: check_compatible first enforces degree, family, length in that order. impl<K: VectorKind> GradedVector<K>::sub.signature: pub fn sub(&self, other: &Self) -> Result<Self, HomologicalError>
impl<K: VectorKind> GradedVector<K>::sub.body: { self.check_compatible(other)?; let coefficients = self .coefficients .iter() .zip(other.coefficients.iter()) .map(|(a, b)| a - b) .collect(); Ok(Self::from_canonical( self.degree, self.basis_id.clone(), coefficients, )) }
impl<K: VectorKind> GradedVector<K>::sub.obligation: The same ordered compatibility gate precedes equal-length pointwise Q subtraction. Canonical field closure and the unchanged degree/family/length justify the internal producer; no clamp, widening or hidden drop.

impl<K: VectorKind> GradedVector<K>::che.body: { if self.degree != other.degree { return Err(HomologicalError::DegreeMismatch { expected: self.degree.value(), got: other.degree.value(), }); } if self.basis_id != other.basis_id { return Err(HomologicalError::BasisMismatch { description: "different graded basis families".into(), }); } if self.coefficients.len() != other.coefficients.len() { return Err(HomologicalError::DimensionMismatch { expected: self.coefficients.len(), got: other.coefficients.len(), }); } Ok(()) }
impl<K: VectorKind> GradedVector<K>::che.obligation: Literal exact comparisons: first unequal signed degree returns expected/actual, then family returns the fixed BasisMismatch, then unequal lengths returns full usize dimensions. VectorMaps compatibility/refusal theorems model this order; kinds are equal statically because other has Self.

impl<K: VectorKind> GradedVector<K>::sca.signature: pub fn scalar_mul(&self, scalar: &Q) -> Result<Self, HomologicalError>
impl<K: VectorKind> GradedVector<K>::sca.body: { super::exact_scalar::admit_coefficients(std::slice::from_ref(scalar))?; Ok(Self::from_canonical( self.degree, self.basis_id.clone(), self.coefficients.iter().map(|c| c * scalar).collect(), )) }
impl<K: VectorKind> GradedVector<K>::sca.obligation: Admit the raw scalar before any operation, even for an empty vector. Multiply every canonical stored coefficient by the admitted canonical Q scalar. Ratio::new/reduce preserves positive reduced denominator and exact arbitrary precision; internal transport removes only a redundant output GCD scan.
